questions.q: What is the clutch’s job in a vehicle with a manual gearbox?
options: To connect and temporarily disconnect the engine from the gearbox
To accelerate the vehicle
To stop the vehicle instead of the brakes
To maintain air pressure in the tyres
questions.explain: The clutch lets you disconnect the engine from the gearbox in order to change gear or stop without switching the engine off.

questions.q: What is the clutch’s “bite point”?
options: The maximum pressure allowed on the clutch pedal
The moment the clutch pedal reaches the floor
The point where the gear lever engages first gear
The moment the vehicle starts to move as you gradually release the pedal
questions.explain: The bite point is the moment the vehicle starts to move as you gradually release the clutch — from there you carry on releasing while gently adding gas.

questions.q: What usually causes early wear and clutch slipping?
options: Keeping a foot on the clutch pedal even when not changing gear
Using neutral at a traffic light
Pressing the clutch fully on every gear change
Driving in too high a gear on a expressway
questions.explain: A foot resting on the pedal, even without pressing it fully, makes the pressure plate slip on the disc and wears it quickly.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical sign of clutch slipping?
options: The brake warning light comes on
The vehicle only shakes when you stop
Engine revs rise without the vehicle accelerating to match, especially on a hill
The steering becomes very heavy
questions.explain: When the clutch is worn and slipping, the engine revs up without the power reaching the wheels properly — most noticeable on a hill or under hard acceleration.

questions.q: What is the difference between a low gear and a high gear in terms of gear ratio?
options: There is no difference except the number on the lever
A high gear always saves more fuel on a climb
A low gear gives high power and low speed; a high gear gives high speed at low engine revs
A low gear gives high speed and little power; a high gear is the opposite
questions.explain: A low gear multiplies the engine’s power at the cost of speed; a high gear allows high speed at low, economical engine revs.

questions.q: When is it correct to change down to a low gear on a steep climb in a manual gearbox?
options: Only after the engine has already lost revs and is struggling
There is no need to change gear on a climb
Early, before the engine struggles to cope with the gradient
Only if there is another vehicle behind you
questions.explain: Change down early, before the engine labours and struggles — not only once it is already starting to lose revs.

questions.q: What can happen if you change gear without pressing the clutch all the way down?
options: Grinding and wear on the gear teeth
The gearbox will heat up faster
The brake warning light will come on
The vehicle will accelerate faster
questions.explain: Changing gear without fully disconnecting the clutch causes grinding and wears the gear teeth.

questions.q: What is the job of neutral (N) in a manual gearbox?
options: To give the highest possible speed
To allow reverse travel
To fully disconnect the link between the engine and the wheels
To slow the vehicle quickly on a descent
questions.explain: In neutral there is no link between the engine and the wheels; the vehicle can roll freely with no power from the engine.

questions.q: What is the torque converter’s job in an automatic gearbox?
options: To transmit power from the engine to the gearbox through fluid, with no direct mechanical link
To split power between the front and rear axles
To let you choose a gear manually with paddle shifters
To mechanically lock the drive shaft in Park
questions.explain: The torque converter is a hydraulic component that transmits power through fluid instead of a mechanical clutch, and it is also what allows creep.

questions.q: Why must you not shift to neutral (N) on a steep descent, even “to save fuel”?
options: Because it wears out the tyres
Because it disconnects the engine brake and leaves all the braking to the brakes alone
Because it turns on the ABS warning light
Because changing gear on a descent is against the law
questions.explain: In neutral there is no engine braking at all, and the vehicle relies entirely on the friction brakes — exactly when they need the most help.

questions.q: What is “creep” in an automatic vehicle?
options: A phenomenon where the vehicle vibrates when stopped
Engine revs dropping below idle
Slow forward or backward movement in D or R when you lift your foot off the brake, without touching the accelerator
An automatic gear change on a climb
questions.explain: Creep comes from the partial connection inside the torque converter: the vehicle moves on its own the moment you lift your foot off the brake, even without touching the accelerator.

questions.q: What is true about Park (P) mode in an automatic gearbox?
options: It is a full substitute for the handbrake, so there is no need to apply it
It mechanically locks the drive shaft, but you should also apply the handbrake
It is identical to neutral (N)
It is meant only for driving downhill
questions.explain: Park mechanically locks the drive shaft, but you should always apply the handbrake too — especially on a gradient.

questions.q: What is engine braking?
options: Switching off the engine to save fuel on a descent
Using the engine’s resistance, with the help of a low gear, to slow the vehicle
Pressing the brake pedal especially hard
Shifting to neutral on a descent
questions.explain: Engine braking uses the engine’s own internal resistance, with the help of a low gear, to slow down without relying only on the brakes.

questions.q: When is it correct to change down to a low gear ahead of a long descent?
options: It makes no difference when you change down
Only partway down, once the speed builds up too much
Before the descent begins, according to the steepness and the speed you want
Only once the brakes already start to smell of burning
questions.explain: Change down before the descent begins — not partway through, when it is already hard to change down safely at high speed.

questions.q: What is the retarder’s job in trucks and buses?
options: To split power between the front and rear axles
To lock the drive shaft when parked
To slow the vehicle without using the ordinary pads and discs
To change gear by itself with no driver input
questions.explain: The retarder is an extra braking system, usually hydraulic or electric, that slows the vehicle without wearing the friction brakes — important mainly on long descents.

questions.q: What is the differential’s job?
options: To lock the drive shaft when parked
To connect and disconnect the engine from the gearbox
To slow the vehicle on a descent
To let the two wheels on the same axle turn at different speeds on a turn
questions.explain: On a turn, the outer wheel travels a longer distance than the inner one; the differential lets them turn at different speeds at the same time.

questions.q: What is the difference between front-wheel drive and rear-wheel drive?
options: Front-wheel drive has no differential at all
There is no practical difference between the two
Rear-wheel drive exists only in trucks
In front-wheel drive the engine drives only the front wheels; in rear-wheel drive it drives only the rear wheels, through a drive shaft
questions.explain: In front-wheel drive the engine and gearbox drive the front wheels directly; in rear-wheel drive power travels through a drive shaft to the rear differential.

questions.q: What is the transfer case’s job in a 4x4 vehicle?
options: To cool the brake fluid
To increase the top speed
To split drive power between the front and rear axles
To change gear by itself
questions.explain: The transfer case in 4x4 vehicles splits power between the two axles, and sometimes also includes a low-range gear for off-road use.

questions.q: A front-wheel-drive vehicle makes a clicking sound on a sharp turn at full steering lock. What does this usually point to?
options: Low tyre pressure
A worn CV joint on the driven front wheel
A worn rear differential
A stuck handbrake
questions.explain: A click on a sharp turn, mainly on the driven front wheel, is a typical sign of a worn CV joint or its torn dust boot.

questions.q: Which sign usually points to a worn differential or wheel bearing, rather than a brake fault?
options: The ABS warning light is on
A noise only when opening a door
A hum or whine that changes with the vehicle’s speed, and not with braking
A vibration only when pressing the brake pedal
questions.explain: A noise that changes with speed and not with braking usually points to a worn differential or wheel bearing, rather than the braking system.

questions.q: What is true about overdrive?
options: It is used only for reverse travel
It is a high gear that allows economical, smooth driving at expressway speed
It is the lowest gear in the gearbox
It exists only in an automatic gearbox
questions.explain: Overdrive is a high gear in which the wheels turn faster than the engine, for economical, smooth driving at high speed.

questions.q: What do paddle shifters help you do?
options: Choose a gear manually and temporarily in an automatic gearbox, without leaving D
Release the handbrake
Drain water from the air brake system
Switch between front-wheel and rear-wheel drive
questions.explain: Paddle shifters are levers behind the steering wheel that let you choose a gear manually and temporarily, for example for engine braking on a descent, without leaving D.
